fact_text: Islamic bank customers often arrive already convinced that earning profit on savings is not for them, so winning current accounts is easier for Meezan than for conventional banks.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In Islamic banking, savings deposits must receive a profit share while current accounts pay nothing, so a current account earns the bank roughly three to four times more per rupee deposited than a savings account.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst credits Meezan's exceptional returns to three pillars: a high share of current account deposits, tight operating costs and strong loan quality, and says they persist only if management keeps these fundamentals.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Illustration: two banks each with PKR 1,000bn of deposits, one with 30% current accounts and one with 50%, would see after-tax profit rise from about PKR 16bn to PKR 27bn, all else equal.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst projects Meezan's total deposits could reach PKR 3.8 to 4 trillion in 2026, with about half in current accounts, based on management guidance and his own estimates.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's 2026 scenario, with an average policy rate near 11%, Islamic financing and investment income is around PKR 440 to 450bn and profit after tax about PKR 95 to 100bn.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The same 2026 scenario gives EPS of about PKR 53 to 55, with other income of PKR 35 to 37bn and admin costs of PKR 85 to 90bn; the analyst stresses these are assumption-based and actual results may differ materially.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Meezan raised its quarterly dividend to PKR 7.5 per share in 2026, which the analyst says implies about PKR 30 for the full year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Until 2024 the State Bank's minimum deposit rate (MDR) did not apply to Islamic bank savings accounts; from 2025 it did, forcing Islamic banks to pay savers roughly 1.5 to 2% more and compressing their margins.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Central bank remittance incentives are a fee paid to banks for formal-channel inflows, so their withdrawal removes a fee income line and slightly reduces bank earnings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Meezan's digital app allows unusually high daily transfer limits, which serves wholesale traders paying suppliers after banking hours and deepens customer loyalty.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues that giving up some transaction fee income for customer loyalty pays off, because loyal customers keep current accounts that earn far more than fees over time.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When borrowers default, banks must book provisions and losses that hit profit directly, so long-run loan recovery matters as much as deposit mix and cost control.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: High interest rates usually lift bank earnings but also raise deposit costs and default risk, so banks tend to trade at lower P/E multiples; falling rates usually support higher multiples, as Buffett's gravity analogy suggests.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rule of thumb is that Meezan has historically traded around 8 to 9 times earnings and 2 to 2.5 times book value across market cycles.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Buying a good company at a P/E far above its usual range can mean a year or more of sideways price action, as earnings growth must pull the multiple back down before the shares move up.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's three-step process is to understand the business first, then verify the numbers, and only then invest.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues that buying PSX during oil-shock corrections has historically rewarded investors over the following few years, while stressing that no return is guaranteed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Rs 1 Trillion Meezan Bank | Is It Still a Buy?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
